Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Brandon King and Johnson Charles are the two openers for West Indies. Anrich Nortje to start proceedings with the ball for South Africa. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

West Indies, on the other hand, were excellent with the ball once again. In this game, it was Shamar Joseph who set the tone by getting rid of Reeza Hendricks early and Obed McCoy followed it up by dismissing Ryan Rickelton. Gudakesh Motie continued his wicket-taking form and got rid of the dangerous QDK. However, then they allowed a bit of a partnership to be built and it was McCoy who got them the important breakthrough. Their catching and fielding were fantastic as well with Motie, Joseph, and McCoy all adding one more wicket to their tallies and closing the innings well. Now, it is up to their batters who will be chasing for the first time in this series but they should be fine but South Africa will hope that their spinners can do the same as the Windies did to them in the last couple of games. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Obed McCoy is up for a quick chat. He says that he bowled pretty well as compared to the previous two games where he went for a few runs. Adds that he wasn't happy with the length last time but things went well on this track and says that he used his off-cutters well and effectively.

South Africa got off to a decent enough start but once again suffered a mini collapse with both Reeza Hendricks and Ryan Rickelton getting out one after the other with Quinton de Kock following suit. Matthew Breetzke also couldn't make much impact. However, it was their skipper Rassie van der Dussen once again who got them out of trouble and found good support from Wiaan Mulder as they added 77 runs together before the latter was dismissed. Their captain continued to attack from one end and notched up a gritty half-century and debutant Patrick Kruger also added a few crucial runs to get them to a respected score.

Another solid bowling performance from West Indies! Despite Rassie van der Dussen's fighting knock, South Africa have been restricted to under 170 here and it will be a challenge for them to defend this in front of the power-packed Windies batting arsenal.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The players of West Indies are already out and have taken their respective fielding positions. The two openers of South Africa are Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks, and the former is taking his guard. West Indies introduce spin right on as Akeal Hosein has the new ball and is all in readiness to get the proceedings underway. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree and Carlos Braithwaite are at the 22 yards. Informs it is equidistant at 64 meters on both squares. Says there's a heavy breeze blowing across the ground and reckons that the bowlers should try to force the batters to hit it into the wind. Carlos Braithwaite joins him and says there has been constant rolling and there's a bit of grass as well and that the moisture is not that much, but thinks that the surface will play much better than the previous games.

Brandon King, the skipper of West Indies says that they played both games on the same track and they know how it will play. Adds Roston Chase played really well and showed how exactly one should play on such a surface. Says the mood in the camp is really positive and hopes that they finish the series on a good note. Informs a couple of changes. Romario Shepherd and Roston Chase are given a rest, Hayden Walsh and Alick Athanaze comes into the XI with the latter making his debut.

Rassie van der Dussen, the South African skipper says that they will bat first. Adds that it is a used wicket and they have seen how it played in the last couple of games. Mentions that their middle order needs to step up. Tells that he knows there is a bit of inexperience but they can't be making excuses. Informs Gerald Coetzee comes in for Lungi Ngidi, and Patrick Kruger makes his debut replacing Andile Phehlukwayo.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King (C), Johnson Charles, Kyle Mayers, Alick Athanaze (In place of Roston Chase and on debut), Andre Fletcher (WK), Fabian Allen, Hayden Walsh (In place of Romario Shepherd), Akeal Hosein, Gudakesh Motie, Shamar Joseph, Obed McCoy.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Ryan Rickelton, Matthew Breetzke, Rassie van der Dussen (C), Wiaan Mulder, Patrick Kruger (In place of Andile Phehlukwayo and on debut), Gerald Coetzee (In place of Lungi Ngidi), Bjorn Fortuin, Nqabayomzi Peter, Anrich Nortje.
TOSS UPDATE - Rassie van der Dussen, the South African skipper calls it right and elects to BAT first.

South Africa, on the other haven't been at their best but they have another opportunity to try out a few things before going into the World Cup. The positive thing for them is that Quinton de Kock is back in form and couple of others like Rassie van der Dussen and Reeza Hendricks have also got some runs. Their bowlers have not been consistent and will be hoping that the likes of Lungi Ngidi, Gerald Coetzee, and Anrich Nortje can get back their rhythm in this game and avoid the clean-sweep. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

West Indies have been really good in this series in all three departments and have outplayed South Africa. Brandon King has led the side really well and it is his first series win captaining his country. Their batting has always been a powerhouse and that was visible in the two games but interestingly it has been the spinners who have stole the show. Gudakesh Motie, Roston Chase, and Akeal Hosein have been excellent and they will want to put on another dominating performance in this game.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 3rd T20I between West Indies and South Africa. The Windies have already sealed the series with two comfortable wins and will look to complete the whitewash while the Proteas will hope that they can atleast end the series on a positive note.
... MATCH DAY ...

The third and final T20I between West Indies and South Africa is here, and this series has provided both teams with a chance to identify areas for improvement ahead of the big event. The hosts have already clinched the series and are now aiming for a clean sweep. Brandon King has led the team well with his decisions and performances with the bat. Johnson Charles hasn't had the best run so far and will look to score big in this game. Kyle Mayers has been fantastic, while Andre Fletcher and Roston Chase have also contributed with the bat. The standout performers, however, have been the spinners, particularly Gudakesh Motie. Akeal Hosein, Fabian Allen, and Roston Chase have also capitalized on the conditions. Shamar Joseph has been somewhat expensive, but Obed McCoy and Romario Shepherd have compensated with effective death bowling. West Indies will want to maintain their momentum and secure another win to boost their confidence going into the World Cup. South Africa, on the other hand, will be disappointed with their performances in the first two games. However, they can take heart from Quinton de Kock's return to form, looking great in the last game, with Reeza Hendricks also maintaining good form. Their middle order has struggled, except for skipper Rassie van der Dussen, and this is a key area for improvement. Their pacers have also been inconsistent and expensive. They will need better performances from Lungi Ngidi, Anrich Nortje, and Gerald Coetzee, while Andile Phehlukwayo is well-suited to these conditions. Two debutants, Ottniel Baartman and Nqabayomzi Peter, have performed well with the ball, and Bjorn Fortuin remains reliable. The Proteas will be playing for pride and will want to end the series with a win to regain confidence and build momentum for the World Cup. In conclusion, this final T20I promises to be an exciting contest. The Windies will aim for a whitewash, while the Proteas will look to salvage some pride with a victory. Fans are eagerly watching to see which team will come out on top in this crucial preparatory match ahead of the World Cup.
